initiative: ShopPilot — a single Thai merchant wants its own B2C web storefront where customers self-serve the full purchase journey (browse -> cart -> checkout -> mock payment -> delivery tracking) and back-office staff manage catalog, stock, orders and coupons from one console, without phone or chat. The MVP must 'actually sell' in a simulated setting (stock reservation, coupon and pre-shipment cancellation rules genuinely enforced), stay extensible to a real payment/shipping provider and a future loyalty program, and double as the team's end-to-end software-delivery (SDLC) workflow testbed.
context: Market: Thailand; single currency (THB); single language. Users: Guest (browse/register), Customer (full self-serve; own-data-only isolation is non-negotiable), Admin (separate back-office role), plus automated system tasks (stock-reservation TTL release, mock payment/shipping status updates, notification + audit logging). Constraints (§7): one sprint; single merchant (not a marketplace); mock payment and shipping providers; web-only; no real email/SMS; demo accounts + seed data. Success signals (§3): registration->first-purchase rate, cart-abandonment and checkout->payment funnel, order-confirm/listing latency, zero stock-mismatch and zero double-charge, full order traceability. Governance already resolved in the gap-closed workshop (§14-§20): PDPA B.E. 2562 lawful basis per PII field with Thailand/Singapore residency and a 5-year Revenue Code retention envelope; Consumer Protection Act / Electronic Transactions Act (total shown before payment, electronic-record confirmation); PCI-DSS v4.0 kept out of cardholder-data scope (PSP-tokenized, no PAN/CVV stored). Source: the gap-closed structured requirement ecommerce_mvp_business_only.gap-closed.md (§1-§20); this discovery framing is derived retrospectively from that document's business narrative (§1-§3) and resolved governance (§14-§20).
